rounds.text: Goyal Aluminiums Ltd trades at an expensive valuation with a P/E ratio of 47.8x and an EV/EBITDA of 23.06x, both of which sit well above sector benchmarks [E1, E11]. Compounding this valuation risk, the company exhibits deteriorating fundamental growth, with trailing twelve-month sales growth at -1% and profit growth contracting by -16% [E16, E19]. Operational cash generation has collapsed into negative territory, evidenced by an operating cash flow of Rs -0.69 Cr and a severe free cash flow burn of Rs -11.74 Cr in Mar 2026 [E32, E33]. Simultaneously, borrowings have surged significantly to Rs 10.68 Cr from just Rs 0.08 Cr a year prior, sharply increasing financial risk alongside weak return metrics such as an 8.13% ROCE that lags the sector [E10, E36]. Market sentiment aligns with these fundamental strains as the stock trades below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a lagging relative-strength rating of 23 [E46, E47]. Conceded: quarterly operating margins show a recent positive trend increasing over the last five quarters alongside strong year-over-year profit spikes [E28, E30, E63].

Conceded: P/E sits at 47.8x and EV/EBITDA is 23.06x [E1, E11]. However, the valuation disconnect ignores a powerful fundamental acceleration visible in the most recent periods, including quarterly operating margins expanding to 8% in Mar 2026—a massive seven percentage point jump year-over-year—marking an increasing trend across five consecutive quarters [E28, E30]. Conceded: TTM sales growth is -1% and TTM profit growth is -16% [E16, E19]. Yet those lagging twelve-month figures completely mask an explosive recent spike where net profit surged +18200% year-over-year alongside an 81% top-line expansion, outstripping the sector's median sales growth [E61, E63, E71]. Conceded: operating and free cash flows are negative for Mar 2026 and borrowings increased to Rs 10.68 Cr [E32, E33, E36]. Nonetheless, the company operates with a moderate debt-to-equity ratio of 0.46x and benefits from a supportive service sector tailwind score of +0.58, while strong multi-year compounding shows a 69% profit growth over five years that vastly outpaces the 15% share price growth [E17, E20, E35, E69]. Conceded: the stock trades below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a 23 relative-strength rating [E46, E47]. This negative price momentum misinterprets a classic turnaround situation where results score a perfect 100/100 and management is expected to deliver a good upcoming quarter, leaving the market's cautious sentiment detached from rapidly improving operational reality [E55, E68].
